# buildkite_cluster_agent_image (Resource)

A custom agent image for Linux hosted agents in a cluster. Buildkite builds the image from a
Dockerfile body on top of its managed hosted agent base image. Reference the built image from a
hosted cluster queue with `hosted_agents.linux.agent_image_ref = buildkite_cluster_agent_image.<name>.image_ref`.

A cluster gets its hosted agents environment when its first hosted queue is created, so the cluster
must already have a hosted queue before an image can be created in it. Use `depends_on` when that
queue is managed in the same configuration.

The API token requires `read_clusters` and `write_clusters` scopes, and its user must have
permission to manage the cluster. This permission is required for reads as well as writes.

Creating an image waits for its build to finish. If the build fails or the wait times out, Terraform
reports an error and retains the image for replacement on the next apply.

This resource does not support in-place updates. Changing `dockerfile` requires replacement:
Terraform deletes the existing image, then re-creates it with the new Dockerfile instructions.
Changing `cluster_id` or `name` also requires replacement.

An image used by a queue cannot be deleted. Before replacing an image, switch all queues that use it
to a different image in a separate apply. After the replacement is built, switch the queues back to
the new image reference in a subsequent apply.

## Example Usage

```terraform
resource "buildkite_cluster" "hosted" {
  name = "Hosted cluster"
}

# A cluster can hold agent images once it has a hosted queue
resource "buildkite_cluster_queue" "default" {
  cluster_id = buildkite_cluster.hosted.id
  key        = "default"

  hosted_agents = {
    instance_shape = "LINUX_AMD64_2X4"
  }
}

resource "buildkite_cluster_agent_image" "ruby" {
  cluster_id = buildkite_cluster.hosted.uuid
  name       = "ruby"

  # Changing dockerfile deletes and re-creates the image; in-place updates are not supported
  # Switch queues to a different image in a separate apply before replacing this image
  dockerfile = <<-EOT
    RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y ruby-full
  EOT

  depends_on = [buildkite_cluster_queue.default]
}

# Run a hosted queue's agents on the image
resource "buildkite_cluster_queue" "ruby" {
  cluster_id = buildkite_cluster.hosted.id
  key        = "ruby"

  hosted_agents = {
    instance_shape = "LINUX_AMD64_2X4"

    linux = {
      agent_image_ref = buildkite_cluster_agent_image.ruby.image_ref
    }
  }
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `cluster_id` (String) The UUID of the cluster the image belongs to.
- `dockerfile` (String) The Dockerfile instructions to build the image with. Buildkite provides the base image, so this must not contain a `FROM` instruction. Changing this attribute requires replacement: the existing image is deleted, then re-created. In-place updates are not supported.
- `name` (String) The name of the agent image. Must be unique within the cluster.

### Optional

- `timeouts` (Block, Optional) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedblock--timeouts))

### Read-Only

- `id` (String) The ID of the agent image.
- `image_ref` (String) The reference of the built image, for a hosted queue's `hosted_agents.linux.agent_image_ref`.
- `status` (String) The build status of the image: `BUILDING`, `READY` or `FAILED`.

<a id="nestedblock--timeouts"></a>
### Nested Schema for `timeouts`

Optional:

- `create` (String) How long to wait for the image to build. Must be greater than zero. Defaults to 30 minutes.

## Import

Using `terraform import`, import resources using the `id`. For example:
```shell
# Import an agent image using {cluster_id}/{image_id} or {cluster_id}/{image_name}.
# Names match exactly and are case-sensitive. An ID match takes precedence over a
# name match. Terraform stores the resolved image ID in state for either form.
#
# You can find the cluster_id under cluster settings in the UI
# and the image_id from the REST API response from:
# GET /v2/organizations/{org_slug}/clusters/{cluster_id}/agent-images
terraform import buildkite_cluster_agent_image.ruby 01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef/snb5nqcik8ge2

# Alternatively, import the same image by name:
terraform import buildkite_cluster_agent_image.ruby '01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef/ruby'
```

In Terraform v1.5.0 and later, use an [`import` block](https://developer.hashicorp.com/terraform/language/import) to import instances using the `id`. For example:
```terraform
# Use cluster_id/image_name or cluster_id/image_id.
import {
  to = buildkite_cluster_agent_image.ruby
  id = "01234567-89ab-cdef-0123-456789abcdef/ruby"
}
```
